merge_ruling.for_merge: The initial L agrees with Liman and both cards are Chicago readings of the summer of 1835.
merge_ruling.against_merge: ONE ISSUE SETS BOTH SPELLINGS IN TWO DIFFERENT COLUMNS, WHICH IS EVIDENCE AGAINST AND NOT FOR. The Democrat of 1 July 1835 prints 'Curtis, Liman' in the post-office return at column 4 and 'L. Curtiss' at column 13 of the same issue. A compositor who set Curtis in one column and Curtiss in another that day was distinguishing two names, not wavering over one; C9 asks for a printing caught setting both spellings FOR ONE MAN and this is a printing caught keeping them apart. L. G. Curtiss is besides set 'L. G. Curtiss' on 22 July and 'Curtiss, L. G.' on 5 August 1835, three settings that never drop the second s, and the town holds curtiss_j beside him. The middle initial G is printed on the Curtiss side and absent on Liman's. D7.
